provenance.canonical-source: packages/core/src/badge/{Badge.tsx,Badge.css,index.ts} — the whole component, three files and 90 lines of CSS. Read for defaults, composition and the documented contract: packages/core/stories/badge/{badge.stories.tsx,badge.qa.stories.tsx} and site/docs/components/badge/{index,usage,examples,accessibility}.mdx. Resolution through packages/theme/css/next/characteristics/{text,sentiment,content}.css, next/palette/{accent,foreground,corner}.css, next/foundations/color.css and packages/theme/css/foundations/{size,spacing,curve,typography,zindex}.css. Reused rather than re-derived: docs/foundations/{typography,sizes,spacing,shape,colors,density,layers}.md.
provenance.pill-bg: Badge.css `background: var(--salt-sentiment-accent-background)` -> next/characteristics/sentiment.css:16 -> --salt-palette-accent -> next/palette/accent.css -> --salt-color-blue-500 -> next/foundations/color.css --salt-color-blue-500-rgb: 0, 120, 207. MODE-INVARIANT: accent.css declares --salt-palette-accent: var(--salt-color-blue-500) under BOTH [data-mode="light"] and [data-mode="dark"]. ACCENT SCOPE TRIM: palette-accent also has a data-accent axis (blue default, teal alternate); this column pins blue, matching button/input/select/dialog/tabs/card.salt.json — only calendar.salt.json models byAccent. Recorded, not modelled.
provenance.pill-fg: Badge.css `color: var(--salt-content-bold-foreground)` -> next/characteristics/content.css:9 -> --salt-palette-foreground-primary-alt -> next/palette/foreground.css, which declares it as --salt-color-white in BOTH the light block (line 4) and the dark block (line 13) -> --salt-color-white-rgb: 255, 255, 255. So a Salt badge is white-on-blue in dark mode too — the whole component is mode-invariant, which no other system's badge is.
provenance.pill-radius: Badge.css `border-radius: var(--salt-palette-corner-strongest, 9999px)` -> next/palette/corner.css, which assigns corner-strongest to --salt-curve-999 = 999px under BOTH [data-corner="rounded"] (line 7) AND [data-corner="sharp"] (line 15), where every other corner stop collapses to curve-0 under sharp. So the badge stays a pill in the sharp corner edition — density-invariant and corner-edition-invariant (foundations/curve.css declares curve-999: 999px in all four density blocks). Matches docs/foundations/shape.md's 'pill/full ... 999px (all editions)'. NOTE: this is the only var() FALLBACK in the whole component; the generated output uses no fallbacks (lesson 1).
provenance.pill-z: Badge.css `z-index: var(--salt-zIndex-default)` -> foundations/zindex.css --salt-zIndex-default: 1, density-invariant. Salt is the only one of the three systems with a shared z-index scale at all (docs/foundations/layers.md).
provenance.byDensity.badge-size: Badge.css declares `--badge-size: var(--salt-text-notation-lineHeight)` on the ROOT .saltBadge and consumes it on the inner pill (`height: var(--badge-size); min-width: var(--badge-size)`). -> next/characteristics/text.css, density blocks .salt-theme-next.salt-density-{high,medium,low,touch}: notation lineHeight 10 / 13 / 16 / 18px. Salt sizes its badge off a TYPE metric rather than off the size scale — which is why the dot form has to override --badge-size itself rather than only a height.
provenance.byDensity.badge-size-dot: Badge.css `.saltBadge-dotBadge { height: var(--salt-size-adornment); min-width: var(--salt-size-adornment); --badge-size: var(--salt-size-adornment) }` -> foundations/size.css --salt-size-adornment: 6 / 8 / 10 / 12px by density (high/medium/low/touch). FROZEN-TOKEN CHECK, run in both directions per lesson 7: size-adornment IS on the DENSITY scale (docs/foundations/sizes.md line 11), so snapshotting the medium 8px would have been wrong at three of four densities. Nothing in this component is on the size-fixed-* or spacing-fixed-* scales.
provenance.byDensity.pill-padding: Badge.css `padding-left: var(--salt-spacing-50); padding-right: var(--salt-spacing-50)` and NO block padding -> foundations/spacing.css spacing-50 = calc(0.5 * spacing-100), with spacing-100 = 4 / 8 / 12 / 16px by density, giving 2 / 4 / 6 / 8px. Source carries a comment on this exact declaration: `/* Should this vary according to touch size */`.
provenance.byDensity.anchor-right: Badge.css `.saltBadge-topRight { right: var(--salt-spacing-100) }` -> foundations/spacing.css spacing-100 = 4 / 8 / 12 / 16px by density. The DOT form overrides this with calc(size-adornment / 2) — see style.badge.anchor@dot.
provenance.byDensity.type-notation: Badge.css `font-size: var(--salt-text-notation-fontSize); font-weight: var(--salt-text-notation-fontWeight); font-family: var(--salt-text-fontFamily); line-height: var(--salt-text-notation-lineHeight)`. -> next/characteristics/text.css: notation fontSize/lineHeight 8/10 . 10/13 . 12/16 . 14/18 by density (high/medium/low/touch); --salt-text-notation-fontWeight: var(--salt-typography-fontWeight-semiBold) = 600 (foundations/typography.css:9); --salt-text-fontFamily: var(--salt-typography-fontFamily-openSans) = 'Open Sans'. Matches docs/foundations/typography.md line 58's caption/notation row (10px/13px at medium). SEMIBOLD is the finding: Salt's badge is the heaviest of the three (600 against shadcn's and M3's 500) and the smallest at 10px.
provenance.no-variant-axis: CONFIRMED ABSENCE, checked against the whole component and its docs: BadgeProps declares exactly three props — `value?: number | string`, `children?: ReactNode`, `max?: number`. There is no variant, appearance, sentiment, tone, status, size, emphasis or disabled prop, and Badge.css declares exactly one background and one colour. A Salt badge is always accent blue. Its usage.mdx makes the omission deliberate: 'To communicate status through color, such as red/amber/green statuses. Instead, use Pill.'
provenance.no-interaction-rules: CONFIRMED ABSENCE: Badge.css contains no :hover, :focus, :focus-visible, :active or disabled selector, and Badge.tsx binds no handler and sets no tabIndex or cursor. usage.mdx states the intent: 'Badges are independent of user action'.
provenance.no-icon-and-no-gap: CONFIRMED ABSENCE: the pill's only child is the formatted value string. There is no icon rule, no gap, no ::before and no ::after in Badge.css.
provenance.children-means-host-not-label: API divergence recorded rather than smoothed: in Salt, `children` is the HOST the badge anchors to and `value` is the label. The chassis separates them (`host` and `value`/`children`) so that shadcn and M3, whose children ARE the label, can share the same component — see docs/BADGE-MATRIX.md's declared approximations.

structure.shell.source: Badge.tsx returns {children}{valueText} — always two spans, even for an inline badge, because .saltBadge is the position:relative context the anchored form absolutely positions out of

structure.label-format.source: Badge.tsx `const valueText = typeof value === "number" && value > max ? `${max}+` : value` — the component formats its own label from a value prop; children mean something else entirely

structure.dot.source: Badge.css .saltBadge-dotBadge + Badge.tsx `const dotBadge = typeof value === "undefined"`; site/docs/components/badge/examples.mdx has dedicated 'Dot badge' and 'Inline dot badge' sections

structure.anchoring.source: Badge.css .saltBadge-topRight + Badge.tsx `[withBaseName("topRight")]: children`; examples.mdx: 'The Badge is anchored to the top-right corner when attached to a child component such as a button'

structure.icon.note: CONFIRMED ABSENCE — no icon rule and no gap anywhere in Badge.css; the pill's only content is the formatted value

prop.content.source: Badge.tsx: `value` is optional and `dotBadge = typeof value === "undefined"`, so a bare <Badge /> renders a DOT. DOT IS THE SOURCE DEFAULT and is therefore value[0] — a label-first list would have made every unqualified Salt badge in the harness render as a pill against source

prop.placement.source: Badge.tsx JSDoc on `children`: 'If a child is provided the Badge will render top right. By defualt renders inline.' (typo in source). Inline is the stated default and is value[0]

prop.variant.note: CONFIRMED ABSENCE — see the no-variant-axis provenance entry. Three props, none of them an appearance axis

prop.interaction.source: single-valued confirmed absence: no handler, no tabIndex, no asChild, no interaction rule in the CSS

prop.max.source: Badge.tsx `{ value, max = 999, ... }` — a single sourced default, not a capability list. usage.mdx: 'If you don't pass a max value to the component, it will truncate the value after three digits displaying 999+ for any values over 999'

behavior.role.value: none — no role and no aria-* on either span
behavior.role.source: Badge.tsx writes className, ref and {...rest} only. accessibility.mdx puts the whole contract on the consumer: 'ensure the focusable element has an aria-label or aria-labelledby attribute that describes the badge, such as "9 notifications"'

behavior.dot-detection.value: inferred from the ABSENCE of a value

behavior.anchor-detection.value: inferred from the PRESENCE of a child

behavior.value-clamping.value: numbers above max render as `${max}+`; strings are never clamped
behavior.value-clamping.source: Badge.tsx `typeof value === "number" && value > max ? `${max}+` : value`; usage.mdx confirms the string half: 'When you pass a string, the badge will not clamp the value'

behavior.activation.source: no onClick, no onKeyDown, no tabIndex, no cursor rule. usage.mdx: 'Badges are independent of user action'; 'To trigger an immediate action ... Instead, use Pill'

behavior.live-region.note: CONFIRMED ABSENCE — no aria-live, aria-atomic or role=status. accessibility.mdx relies on the badge being read when navigated to ('the screen reader automatically announces the contents of the badge'), so a Salt badge whose count changes while unfocused announces nothing

slot.host.source: badge.stories.tsx Icon/MaxNumber/DefaultTruncation/String/MultipleButtons/DotBadge all pass a <Button> with an icon as children. DECLARED COMPOSITION to `button` and to an icon set

state.rest.value: accent blue fill, white label — MODE-INVARIANT in both properties
state.rest.note: the only badge of the three that looks identical in dark mode

state.hover.note: CONFIRMED ABSENCE — no :hover selector in Badge.css

state.focus.note: CONFIRMED ABSENCE — no :focus or :focus-visible selector; the badge is never focusable

style.badge.letter-spacing.note: CONFIRMED ABSENCE — Badge.css declares no letter-spacing

style.badge.size.source: Badge.css `height: var(--badge-size); min-width: var(--badge-size)` with --badge-size = text-notation-lineHeight

style.badge.overflow.note: CONFIRMED ABSENCE — no overflow rule. usage.mdx handles long labels in PROSE instead: 'avoid using a badge with more than four to six characters. If needed, truncate strings exceeding this count with an ellipsis' — a consumer instruction, not a component rule

style.badge.margin.source: Badge.css `margin: auto` on the pill. The pill is a flex item of the inline-flex .saltBadge wrapper, so auto centres it on the cross axis; it is deliberately NOT promoted to the chassis base, because on shadcn's and M3's wrapper-less badges an auto margin in a consumer flex row would absorb free space and push them apart

style.badge.transition.note: CONFIRMED ABSENCE — no transition and nothing that changes

style.badge.dot.source: Badge.css `.saltBadge-dotBadge { height: var(--salt-size-adornment); min-width: var(--salt-size-adornment); padding: 0; --badge-size: var(--salt-size-adornment) }`. The --badge-size redeclaration is ON THE PILL, not on the wrapper, and that placement is load-bearing: style.badge.anchor's translateY reads --badge-size on the element the transform applies to (lesson 2). Reproduced with the same placement

style.badge.anchor.source: Badge.css `.saltBadge-topRight { position: absolute; right: var(--salt-spacing-100); transform: translateX(100%) translateY(calc(-1 * (var(--badge-size) / 2))) }`. No `top` is declared — the vertical placement is the static position plus a half-height lift

style.badge.anchor@dot.source: Badge.css `.saltBadge-dotBadge.saltBadge-topRight { right: calc((var(--salt-size-adornment) / 2)) }` — the dot sits half its own width in, where the labelled form sits a full spacing-100 in
